sources.entry: Will Be Done - Offline-first task manager with weekly planning, project boards, real-time sync, Vim keybindings, desktop quick add, and import from popular task managers (alternative to TickTick, Todoist). (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Will Be Done is an offline-first, self-hosted task planner built around a visual weekly timeline with a persistent Stash focus list, Vim-style keybindings, and real-time sync.
summary.what_it_does: It lets you collect tasks, place them on a daily/weekly timeline, organize them into projects with ordered sections, and keep a persistent Stash list of focus tasks available from any page. Tasks support descriptions, checklists, scheduling, and recurring templates (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly with custom intervals and end rules). The browser keeps a full local database so reads and writes work offline, and changes sync across tabs and devices when the server is reachable. The self-hosted server runs in Docker and stores data in SQLite by default, with an HTTP API documented at /api/docs and bearer-token auth. The README also describes a desktop app with a global quick-add shortcut and import from Todoist (API token) and TickTick (CSV export).
use_cases: weekly task planning on a visual timeline
self-hosted task manager with data ownership
importing tasks from Todoist or TickTick
how_to_run: Open the server in a browser at the mapped port (http://localhost:3000)
pnpm dev:server and pnpm dev:client in separate terminals (development)
notable: Visual weekly timeline where each day is a column, with drag-and-drop rebalancing
Offline-first: full browser-side database with changes applied without a server round trip
Vim-style keybindings for navigation and task actions
Stash: a persistent focus list available from every page
Self-hosting in one Docker command with SQLite, no Redis or S3 required
caveats: Mobile is currently a PWA; iOS and Android app store builds are only planned
Several listed features are roadmap items, not yet available (CLI app, undo/redo, notifications, end-to-end encryption, global search)
Multi-user spaces and shared tasks are explicitly not planned
